cards.questionText:
Dear High View Apartments Residents,

Please be advised that Riverside Paving Company will be at High View Apartments on May 3 and 4 to repave the parking lot. To allow the work to begin on schedule, all vehicles must be removed from the parking area by 8:00 A.M. on May 3. Residents will be able to use the parking lot again starting at 8:00 A.M. on May 5.

We understand that finding alternative parking may be inconvenient. However, removing all vehicles is essential to ensure the project can be completed within the planned two-day period.

Please note that all parking spaces will be expanded in width, and some spaces may be relocated as part of the resurfacing work. If your assigned parking space is moved more than 20 meters from its current location, you will be notified by email.

Thank you for your understanding and cooperation.

Judith Alvarez
Property Manager

cards.questionText:
Refurbished Theater Gives Town a Boost

BEACHVILLE (February 24) - Residents of Beachville and visiting tourists have something exciting to look forward to. The Crown Coastal Theater, which has been a part of the community for 40 years, is expected to reopen in June.

Many people were disappointed when the theater's previous owners shut it down more than a year ago because the building required costly renovations. Thankfully, new owners have taken over and spent the past year improving both the interior facilities and the projection equipment.

According to Christine Lafferty, she and her longtime friend Morgan Flanagan spent much of their childhood at the theater. “Watching movies was a favorite activity on rainy days in a coastal town like ours. We were very disappointed when it closed,” she said.

Lafferty and Flanagan, who are also the owners of the well-known Blue Bay Bistro, purchased the theater and carried out the repairs needed to ensure it remains a successful and vibrant business.

For additional details about the theater and upcoming events, visit www.crowncoastaltheater.com.

cards.questionText:
Vimalo Brands Enters a New Era

By Yvette Maurer

VANCOUVER (2 August) - Vimalo Brands, a major consumer goods company known for its nutritional supplements and personal-care products such as Powerburst breakfast beverages and Honeysoft soaps and lotions, is preparing to introduce a new product category: frozen foods. "Our new Nutridinna line is not just about convenience," CEO Danitza Martens said during a press conference earlier today. She explained that while frozen foods are not a new idea, the company’s flash-freezing technique preserves the natural texture, flavour, vitamins, and minerals of fresh meat and produce. This allows customers to enjoy the ease of frozen meals without compromising quality.

The company has also formed partnerships with farms in the Vancouver region to source ingredients for the Nutridinna range. According to Martens, sourcing locally reduces transportation delays and enables vegetables to be flash-frozen immediately after harvest, when they are at peak freshness. She added that this approach also benefits consumers, as the products can be stored in freezers for up to six months. Nutridinna frozen foods are scheduled to arrive in supermarkets in November, with frozen seafood products expected to be introduced in early next year.

options: To explain a food preparation method
To describe a company merger
To announce a new product line

childQuestions.explanationVi: “Vimalo Brands ... is preparing to introduce a new product category: frozen foods.”, “Nutridinna frozen foods are scheduled to arrive in supermarkets in November.” => Những phát biểu này cho thấy bài báo đang thông báo về dòng sản phẩm thực phẩm đông lạnh mới của công ty.

cards.questionText:
NEW HAVEN (June 1) - Marco’s Italian Restaurant on Frontage Road is scheduled to reopen in late June. It was shut down three months earlier following a water leak that severely damaged the kitchen. The incident required extensive repairs in both the kitchen and dining areas. [1]. When it reopens, the restaurant will be able to host larger groups of customers.

Over the past three months, many staff members were able to continue working at Marco’s Italian Market, located across the street. [2]. “The leak occurred just before the market’s busy season began,” said Tom Marco, who owns both businesses. “We had to temporarily increase staff there, and I was glad to keep my restaurant employees working.” Most of these workers have now returned to their positions at the restaurant.  [3]. 

Mr. Marco has organized a grand reopening event for June 25. The occasion will feature live music and a new tasting menu. [4]. Customers must make reservations for the celebration in advance by calling 203-555-0124. “We are excited to resume preparing our traditional dishes and to welcome the community back,” Mr. Marco said.
